about: Species interactions. Each rule: [actor, target, kind, weight 0-1, what the tap card says, source]. actor/target: a species key, m:<body type> (e.g. m:cera), *pred, *herb or * (any). kinds: hunts (preferred prey, weight raises the pick chance; works for land and sea predators, and makes birds of prey circle low over the target), scavenges (goes to fresh carcasses of target; vultures, condors and eagles circle low over them), follows (moves with target, on land, at sea and in the air), avoids (keeps away from target, on land and at sea), rivals (fights target when close), mobs (approaches a predator as a group and drives it off: baboons at leopards, elephants at lions, humpbacks at killer whales), cleans (sea: small fish hover at the target, like cleaner wrasse on mantas and turtles), schools (sea: swims along with others of the target, as shoals and pods), rings (herd closes into a defensive ring facing the target predator, calves inside, and the predator may give up: muskoxen against wolves, bison, elephants and buffalo). Weights reflect how common the interaction really is. Fossil rules name their evidence (bite marks, stomach contents, wounds) or say 'inferred'.
